data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves, approximately 6-8, are clearly visible radiating from the same node at the apex of the stem)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are concentrated at the shoot tip, while the lower stem appears bare)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (leaves are undivided laminae)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (leaf margins appear smooth and continuous, despite some holes present)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (leaves are significantly longer than wide, with the widest point below the middle and tapering to the apex)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (the tip tapers gradually into a distinct, slender point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (the base tapers into the petiole, appearing wedge-shaped)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a distinct central midrib is visible with secondary veins branching off it)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): clearly visible, parallel to the midrib, and spaced at regular intervals
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (the leaf surface reflects light, indicating a smooth, glossy texture)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (the surface appears smooth without visible hairs)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are visible but distinctively short relative to the leaf blade length)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles appear cylindrical and rounded in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (the stem appears rigid and brown, typical of a hardy seedling)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (the stem surface appears smooth)
    19. Stem color: brown (the visible portion of the stem is a light brown color)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (the stem surface does not show obvious ridges or lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are visible at the leaf attachment points)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: Several leaves exhibit irregular holes and missing tissue along the margins and mid-sections. The leaves are arranged in a dense whorl at the apex of the seedling.
